rules.statement: A subsequent instrument, even though registered at a time before the grantor acquired his title, would prevail over an unregistered deed if the competing instrument remained unregistered at the time of the acquisition of title.
rules.supporting_quote: "Thus, when a deed of transfer of immovable property is executed at a time when the grantor has no title to the property, the subsequent acquisition of title by the grantor would not only give the benefit of such title to the instrument already executed but would also give the grantee the benefit of priority by the registration of that instrument; if the competing instrument remained unregistered at the time of the acquisition of title, the subsequent instrument, even though it was registered at a time before the grantor acquired his title, would prevail over the unregistered deed."

meta.parties: The Colombo Apothecaries Company Limited v. Peiris
